tasks.short: Adapt and submit set plans for approval

steps.what: Adapt the set or exhibit plans to intended purpose, budget and fabrication restrictions using the drawing editor
inputs: known purpose, budget and fabrication restrictions

steps.what: Check the complete revised plans against restrictions and select the exact plan package for submission
inputs: known purpose, budget and fabrication restrictions
outputs: checked final plan package and approval destination

steps.what: Submit the checked final plan package to the internal production lead for approval
inputs: checked final plan package and approval destination

steps.what: Review the submitted plans and decide whether they meet the production's purpose, budget and fabrication restrictions
outputs: approval decision or requested plan changes

tasks.design: Configure native drawing constraints and reusable components in the design editor {OTHER} to assist plan revisions. The designer checks the completed package, submits the exact version through {EMAIL}, and the production lead retains approval authority; requested changes start another checked revision cycle.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plan revisions require repetitive drawing edits as well as creative decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native dimensions, reusable components and drawing constraints can reduce repetitive edits.
tasks.still_hard: Budget compliance does not establish stage practicality or creative suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile artistic purpose with fabrication and use.

ambition.what: No additional production promised from unmeasured revision savings.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: drawing editors can reuse components and enforce dimensions, while creative adaptation and production approval remain human.

assumptions: OTHER is the drawing and set-design editor. Boundary is one plan-adaptation and approval cycle; approval rejection repeats that cycle rather than silently committing unapproved revisions. No fabrication release is performed.

The designer supplies current plans; production supplies purpose, budget and fabrication constraints as existing review inputs. Missing dimensions or cost constraints require manual clarification within revision effort; no model infers them.

Native drawing configuration first. Shares are provisional scenarios. Focal baseline is 90, remaining 79.5; gross 11.67% minus 1 upkeep gives 10.67% net. Production lead's 10 share remains fully retained and outside the focal denominator.
Final designer checking is existing design quality work, not a new sign-off meeting. The short send receives 1 share fully retained. Any edit after s2 invalidates the submission gate.
unknowns: Actual revision workload and editor capabilities
Who holds production approval authority locally
research_questions: Which repeated drawing edits can native constraints reduce without reducing design or fabrication checks?

already_counted.description: Review assisted revisions and check final plan package

incremental.description: Maintain reusable drawing components and restrictions

approvals.approved_version: checked final plan package and internal destination from s2; changed package voids gate

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native tools are already used; up to 7% net where revision gains are smaller than the central 10.67% net scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Exchange set information at rehearsals and meetings

steps.what: Attend rehearsals to observe set use and obtain and share information related to sets
outputs: firsthand understanding of set use and clarified concerns

steps.what: Attend production meetings to obtain and share set information with production colleagues
inputs: firsthand understanding of set use and clarified concerns
outputs: shared set information and clarified production requirements

tasks.design: Keep firsthand rehearsal observation and production discussion with the designer. {PROJECT} reference access cannot replace observing how the set works during rehearsal; this statement establishes no separate minutes, report or send to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical issues emerge while people use the set.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing production tools can hold references but do not remove this observation.
tasks.still_hard: Notice an issue that nobody has yet expressed as a clear requirement.
tasks.human_edge: See how performance and set interact and ask a useful question immediately.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: rehearsal observation and production discussion depend on actual set use and participants' concerns.

assumptions: Boundary covers the statement's rehearsal and production meeting attendance and live information exchange. No separately authored note or report is established; plan revisions are modeled in their own task.
No structured capture contract or tool change is introduced. Native project reference views were considered but do not replace the observed work.
The rehearsal/meeting split is an unmeasured illustrative allocation with no effect on zero savings. No incremental upkeep follows from no change.
unknowns: Whether actual attendance includes separate authored minutes or drawing changes
research_questions: Observe one rehearsal and meeting to identify any distinct record write rather than assuming one.

incremental.description: No introduced tool or record work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Firsthand observation and live exchange remain fully retained; no distinct administrative workload is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clarify exhibit requirements with clients and staff

steps.what: Confer with clients and staff about exhibit space, themes, content, timelines, budgets, materials and promotion requirements
inputs: client and staff accounts of exhibit requirements
outputs: clarified exhibit requirements and unresolved questions

tasks.design: Keep the requirements conversation with the designer. A {PROJECT} intake form may hold existing facts, but does not establish less conversational work or justify an invented briefing-document baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stakeholders may have different purposes and constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project tools can store facts; agreement still needs discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Find contradictory requirements before design starts.
tasks.human_edge: Probe an ambiguous request and reconcile competing priorities.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a requirements form cannot replace clarification of conflicting exhibit constraints.

assumptions: Boundary is conferring to gather the listed information. No distinct written brief, record write or send is stated; do not manufacture one to claim saving.
Inputs are participants' actual accounts and existing context, not an assumed structured intake. Native forms were considered but no reduction of the live task is established.
No software change or upkeep. The full retained share is the whole task, not an observed time baseline.
unknowns: Whether a written requirements brief is actually produced during this task
research_questions: Does observation reveal a separately timed brief write or fact lookup that should be decomposed?

incremental.description: No new tool or recording process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The specified live requirements discussion remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find source material on architectural and stylistic elements of the period using library and archive catalogues
inputs: existing library and archive catalogue records

steps.what: Examine source context and judge which architectural and stylistic elements are appropriate to the depicted period
outputs: source-grounded selection and remaining historical questions

steps.what: Consult experts as necessary to clarify uncertain architectural or stylistic details
inputs: source-grounded selection and remaining historical questions
outputs: clarified historical interpretation or acknowledged uncertainty

tasks.design: Use native date, geography and collection filters in library and archive search {OTHER} to narrow source retrieval. The designer reads the actual sources, judges suitability and consults experts where the evidence remains unclear; no generated period facts replace research.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source retrieval can involve repeated broad searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue facets can restrict searches by period and collection.
tasks.still_hard: An image may depict a later reconstruction rather than the claimed period.
tasks.human_edge: Read provenance and decide which detail supports the production's setting.

ambition.what: No new research service before measuring retrieval effort.

reach.task: Describe provenance for selected production references

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: archive catalogue filters can narrow historical source retrieval, while period attribution requires source examination.

assumptions: OTHER is library and archive search. Boundary covers retrieval, evaluation and expert consultation, not creation of a separate research report or design drawing.
Archives supply existing catalogue IDs, dates, provenance and images; the designer supplies the period and setting. Missing dates require source examination within s2, not invented metadata.
Native search first. Shares describe an unmeasured research cycle including an expert consultation where necessary; expert labour itself is not transferred into focal savings.
Gross 7 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 6.5 net. All source evaluation and expert discussion remains fully retained.
unknowns: Actual catalogue filter quality and retrieval time
research_questions: Do available catalogue facets reduce search time while preserving conflicting period evidence?

already_counted.description: Check relevance of retrieved source records

incremental.description: Maintain useful catalogue searches as collections change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero for poorly indexed collections; up to 4% if retrieval gains are less than the central 6.5% net scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The designer keeps creative and historical judgement while native tools assist revisions and source retrieval.
reach: Describe provenance for selected references with an archivist
role.ambitious_version: Evidence-backed period design with practical production approval and firsthand rehearsal involvement.
